title: Decide: should JMAP Chat engage with DIDs?
description:
Pure design decision bead, no implementation pending.

Question: should JMAP Chat formally engage with Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs, RFC W3C DID-Core) as a principal type alongside ChatContact.id?

Potential touchpoints if yes:
- ChatContact identity may carry a DID alongside the opaque server-assigned id
- Mentions may have a DID-scoped form (`@{did}` or similar)
- Federation peer authentication may bind to DID rather than (or alongside) the current `ownerUserId` mailbox-owner string
- Push payloads may carry DID identifiers
- New capability URN `urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat:did` possible

Reasons to engage:
- Aligns JMAP Chat with the broader decentralized-identity ecosystem (AT Protocol / Bluesky, fediverse-adjacent projects, W3C VC stack)
- Provides a stable identifier that survives mailbox-server changes
- Future-proofs against post-mailbox identity systems

Reasons to not engage:
- DIDs add operational complexity (method resolution, key rotation, revocation)
- JMAP Chat's federation model is mailbox-server-bound; DIDs assume server-neutral identity
- Increases the surface a JMAP Chat server must understand (DID method registries, etc.)
- The benefit may be deliverable via a separate companion document rather than baking DIDs into the core spec

Decision required: yes, no, or "yes but as a separate companion draft". This bead exists to be answered, not to track implementation. Implementation work, if any, would be filed as separate epics blocked on this decision.
close_reason: Option B \u2014 minimal engagement via one prose sentence acknowledging DID URIs as valid ChatContact.id form. No companion draft, no new capability.
